blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: The Imaginary Dimension
blocks.content: What's the square root of -1? In the real number world, it doesn't exist. But mathematicians invented a magical number called **i** (imaginary unit) where i^2 = -1. A **Complex Number** combines a real part and an imaginary part: **z = a + bi**. It's like adding a second dimension to the number line, creating a whole number PLANE instead of just a line.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Arithmetic with Complex Numbers
blocks.content:
• **Addition:** Add real parts together, add imaginary parts together. (3+2i) + (1+4i) = 4+6i.
• **Subtraction:** Same idea but subtract. (3+2i) - (1+4i) = 2-2i.
• **Multiplication:** Use FOIL, remembering i^2 = -1. (2+3i)(1+i) = 2+2i+3i+3i^2 = 2+5i-3 = -1+5i.
• **Conjugate:** The conjugate of a+bi is a-bi. You flip the sign of the imaginary part.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Finding the Modulus
blocks.content:
The **Modulus** of a complex number z = a + bi is its distance from the origin.

1. Use the formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2).
2. Square the real part.
3. Square the imaginary part (just the coefficient, not the i).
4. Add them together.
5. Take the square root.

This is essentially Pythagoras' Theorem on the complex plane!

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Multiplying Complex Numbers
blocks.content:
Calculate (3 + 2i)(4 - i).

**Step 1 (FOIL):**
First: 3 * 4 = 12
Outer: 3 * (-i) = -3i
Inner: 2i * 4 = 8i
Last: 2i * (-i) = -2i^2

**Step 2:** Combine: 12 - 3i + 8i - 2i^2
**Step 3:** Since i^2 = -1: -2(-1) = +2
**Step 4:** 12 + 2 + 5i = **14 + 5i**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The single most common error: forgetting that i^2 = -1, not +1! When you multiply 2i * 3i, you get 6i^2 = 6(-1) = -6, NOT +6. Every time you see i^2 in your working, immediately replace it with -1. If you miss this step, your real and imaginary parts will both be wrong.
